correctness.rationale: Take \(X=\ell_1(\Gamma)\), which is an \(L_1\)-space even for arbitrary \(\Gamma\). Cheng--Wang--Xiang's sharp \(L_1\) estimate therefore gives the same forward bound used in Wang's finite-coordinate corollary, and Wang's all-Banach quotient duality yields the \(X^*=\ell_\infty(\Gamma)\) adjoint lifting with constant \(22\). For a continuous selector, the closed relation \(R=\{(g,h):Ah=Bg\}\) with norm \(\max\{\|g\|,\|h\|/22\}\) makes projection onto \(g\) a metric quotient with Banach constant one; quantitative Bartle--Graves gives a continuous positive-homogeneous right inverse with arbitrary \(1+\varepsilon\) loss, and symmetrization makes it odd without increasing the bound. For odd \(m\), Wang's parity character has \(D_{\rm sgn}F=0\) but \(D_{\rm long}F\ne0\); Hahn--Banach plus adjoint pairing produces an unsolvable datum.
